questions.question: When you leave your vehicle unattended, you must:

options.text: Lock the ignition and remove the key.

questions.explanation: When you leave your vehicle unattended, turn off the engine, lock the ignition, remove the key, and set the parking brake.

questions.question: What is the most effective way to reduce your risk of injury or death in a crash?

options.text: Stay in the right lane on multilane highways.
Limit your driving to between 3:00 p.m. and 6:00 p.m.

questions.explanation: Wearing your seat belt is the single most effective way to reduce your risk of death or injury while driving.

questions.question: You are entering a busy freeway. What should you do to merge into traffic?

options.text: Use your side and rearview mirrors and check your blind spots.
Use the acceleration lane to match the speed of freeway traffic.
Yield to traffic already on the freeway.

questions.explanation: Use the entrance ramp to speed up and match freeway traffic. Yield to cars already on the freeway. Check your mirrors and blind spots before merging to make sure you have space to merge safely.

questions.question: When you are in a travel lane on the roadway:

options.text: You may stop to drop off passengers.
You may stop to look up an address.
You may make a U-turn or back up if you miss a freeway exit.
Don't stop for any reason. Keep moving until you can safely pull off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Don't stop for any reason. Keep moving until you can safely pull off the road.
questions.explanation: Never stop in a travel lane. Keep driving until you can safely pull off the road. If you miss your turn or exit, do not back up. Continue to the next turn or exit.

questions.question: How does lack of sleep affect your driving compared to other factors?

options.text: The same as driving with teenagers.

questions.explanation: Lack of sleep and alcohol have similar effects on driving ability. Being awake for 18 hours impairs driving about as much as a 0.05 percent blood alcohol level. Being awake for 24 hours impairs driving about as much as a 0.10 percent blood alcohol level.

questions.question: A person's driving ability can be affected by:
questions.explanation: Safe driving depends on being in good physical condition. Alcohol, legal and illegal drugs, and drowsiness can all affect driving ability.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that traffic is entering the road from the right.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. They alert drivers to upcoming hazards. This sign means the divided highway is ending.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, you should:

options.text: Stay calm and move out of the aggressive driver's way.
Flash your lights to show the aggressive driver they are wrong.
Do something aggressive back to the driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay calm and move out of the aggressive driver's way.
questions.explanation: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, stay calm and get out of their way. Trying to get even with an aggressive driver can make the situation more dangerous.

questions.question: You have a green light at an intersection, but pedestrians are crossing against the red. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrians.
Stop to let the pedestrians cross safely.
Drive close to the pedestrians to scare them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop to let the pedestrians cross safely.
questions.explanation: Always yield to pedestrians and any vehicles in the intersection, even when you have a green light. Always be careful around pedestrians.

questions.question: When you see other drivers acting angry around you, what should you do?
questions.explanation: When other drivers are angry, move away from them. Do not look at them or make gestures. Slow down, move to another lane, or do whatever is safe to stay out of danger.

questions.question: Why is night driving harder than daytime driving?

options.text: You cannot see as far in the dark.
You see more motorcycles at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see as far in the dark.
questions.explanation: At night, you can see less of the road. Always use your headlights. Drive slowly enough to stop within the distance you can see ahead.

questions.question: What is important to remember when driving on wet roads?

options.text: Roads are most slippery right when rain starts.

questions.explanation: Wet roads are dangerous, especially when rain first starts. Your tires rest on a layer of water, oil, and dirt. Slow down in rain, standing water, or slush to keep your tires from slipping.

questions.question: You are borrowing an unfamiliar car from a friend. What should you do?

options.text: Not worry about it because all cars are the same.
Do not tell your friend you are unfamiliar with the car.
Ignore any problems to avoid upsetting your friend.
Take a few minutes to learn where all the controls are and how to use them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes to learn where all the controls are and how to use them.
questions.explanation: Before driving an unfamiliar car, find the turn signals, hazard lights, headlights, wipers, brakes, gear shift, and horn. Fix any problems before driving.

questions.question: If a flagger is directing traffic at a construction site, you must:

options.text: Follow what the flagger tells you to do.
Do what other cars are doing, even if the flagger says something else.
Assume the flagger should not be directing traffic.
Follow the normal road rules as if construction was not happening.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow what the flagger tells you to do.
questions.explanation: Slow down and follow the directions of flaggers and signs in construction zones. Not following them is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: When changing lanes on a highway, you should:

options.text: Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.

questions.explanation: Always signal before changing lanes. Check both mirrors and look over your shoulder to see your blind spot.

questions.question: You must stop at a railroad crossing when:

options.text: A flagger tells you to stop.
Red lights are flashing and gates are down.

questions.explanation: Stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger tells you to, when a stop sign is there, or when red lights flash and gates are down.

questions.question: When driving on highways, you should:
questions.explanation: Stay alert on highways and be ready to react to dangers. Avoid staring at one thing too long to prevent highway hypnosis.

questions.question: A driver entering the road from a driveway or private road:

options.text: Must let cars on the road go first.
Can expect other drivers to move for them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must let cars on the road go first.
questions.explanation: If you are coming from a driveway or private road, let traffic on the public road pass first. Merge when it is safe.

questions.question: Motorcycles are allowed to use:

options.text: A full lane like other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: A full lane like other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have the right to use the same full lane width as all other vehicles.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Construction workers on or near the road.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. They warn drivers about hazards ahead. This sign tells you that pedestrians may cross the road ahead.

questions.question: The best way to avoid hydroplaning is to:

options.text: Slow down when roads are wet or slushy.
Watch for standing water or puddles.

questions.explanation: When roads are wet, your car takes longer to stop and may skid when turning quickly. Do not use cruise control on wet or icy roads. Reduce your speed and drive carefully.

questions.question: When it begins to rain while you are driving, you should:

options.text: Drive faster than traffic around you.
Drive at the maximum posted speed limit.
Drive close behind the car in front of you.

questions.explanation: Heavy rain makes it hard to see. Slow down and turn on your headlights so others can see you. If rain is so heavy you cannot see clearly, pull to the shoulder and stop until it passes.

questions.question: When parents or guardians sign the consent form for their teenager's learner license, they are saying that:

options.text: Their child passed a driver education course.
Their child is a careful driver.
Their child's date of birth on the form is correct.
They will pay for any damage caused by the teenager driving a vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: They will pay for any damage caused by the teenager driving a vehicle.
questions.explanation: A parent or guardian must sign a consent form for a teenager under 18 to get a learner license. By signing, they agree to pay for any damage caused by the teenager driving a vehicle.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Reduce speed when the road is wet.
The road ahead has sharp turns or curves.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce speed when the road is wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road is slippery when wet. In wet conditions, slow down, avoid sudden braking or turning, and stay farther away from the car ahead of you.

questions.question: Drinking alcohol and driving is:

options.text: Safe if you have only had a few drinks.

questions.explanation: Driving while impaired by alcohol or drugs is very dangerous. You cannot drive safely if you drink alcohol or use drugs. It puts you and everyone on the road at risk.

questions.question: When you see a steady red traffic light, you should:

options.text: Drive through if there is no crossing traffic.
Keep driving because you have the right-of-way.
Stop only if a police officer is nearby.

questions.explanation: A steady red light means you must stop completely. Running a red light is illegal and very dangerous. You may turn right on red if there is no sign that says otherwise.

questions.question: Braking distance is affected by:

options.text: How fast your vehicle is going.
The condition of your brakes and tires.
The condition of the road surface.

questions.explanation: Braking distance depends on how fast you are going, the condition of your brakes and tires, and the condition of the road surface.

questions.question: You must stop your vehicle:

options.text: At an intersection with a stop sign.
When a traffic officer tells you to stop.

questions.explanation: You must stop at stop signs, at red lights, and whenever a traffic officer orders you to stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop completely and look for pedestrians and crossing traffic.
Stop completely and wait for a green light.
Slow down and check for traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and look for pedestrians and crossing traffic.
questions.explanation: An eight-sided sign is a stop sign. You must stop completely and check for pedestrians and crossing traffic. Wait until the intersection is clear before going.
